summary: An empty peer card is now counted as an empty peer card, not reported as a failed read.
details: nora_peer_card_empty_total was incremented by nora/engagement/context.py but never declared in nora/obs/metric_specs.py, so Metrics.inc fell past its counter branch to a bare self._gauges[name] lookup and raised KeyError. That raise happens inside _peer_card's own `except Exception`, which logs 'peer-card read failed' and increments nora_errors_total{stage="peer_card"} - so the one counter whose purpose is to separate 'her card is genuinely empty' from 'the read failed' reported every genuinely empty card as a transport failure. Inverted, not merely missing.
Confirmed against the running container before the fix: the series was absent from /metrics entirely while the code that writes it runs on every tagged turn.

The instance was one line. The defect was that nothing compared call sites against the declaration tuple, so tests/architecture/test_every_recorded_metric_is_declared.py now does - resolving string literals, module-level constants and conditionals over them across 283 recording call sites (269 resolvable name reads, 144 distinct names).

The set of recording methods is DERIVED, not listed: a forwarding wrapper is any method whose first non-self parameter is passed as the first positional argument to a Metrics recording method. Hand-listing was tried first and a reviewer immediately found two wrappers it had missed - nora/presence/collector.py::_count and nora/infra/sql/entities.py::_set, eight increment sites read by neither test, under a comment claiming they were covered. The derivation finds all nine real wrappers and correctly refuses the same-named status wrappers in nora/agent/relay.py and nora/language/knowledge_search.py, whose first argument is an R-27 status rather than a metric name; adding those by name would have produced roughly forty false offenders.
limitations: The gate reads metric names statically. A site whose name it cannot resolve is pinned in an explicit allowlist rather than skipped, so a NEW unresolvable site fails the gate instead of passing unchecked. The pin is keyed on the argument's source text as well as its location, so a computed name added inside an already-pinned wrapper is caught rather than inheriting that row's excuse.
One genuine gap remains and is pinned: nora/instructions/reload.py binds its metric name at construction (a constructor kwarg), so its two names are not checked by this gate.

The gate checks metric NAMES only, not labels. Metrics._full_labels defaults a missing label to "" and silently drops an undeclared one, so a call site passing a label the spec does not declare is still unreported by anything.

nora_peer_card_empty_total still cannot say WHY a card was empty. HonchoClient._get catches every transport failure and returns None, so a dead endpoint, a timeout, a 4xx, an unknown peer and a genuinely empty card all reach this counter identically - and an outage lands here rather than in nora_errors_total{stage="peer_card"}. Separating them needs a port change.
